questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a height of 9 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 16 × 9 = 72 cm². Halving is the step rushing skips.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A cylinder has radius 4 cm. What is the area of one circular end?

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: The area of a circle is πr², so with radius 4 cm the end area is π × 4² = 16π cm². Doubling the radius instead of squaring it is a common slip.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a sealed container, 24g of reactants react completely. What is the mass of the products?
questions.why: In a closed system, mass is conserved — the products must total the same 24g as the reactants.

questions.prompt: What is it called when a reaction releases heat and makes things feel warmer?
